finding: compile_qubo_projection claims an exact WorldSlice boundary but uses isinstance(source_slice, WorldSlice). A WorldSlice subclass can override sha256(), pass the boundary, and cause source_slice_sha256 in the emitted QuboProjection to be attacker-controlled rather than the canonical digest of the exact WorldSlice value.
counterhypothesis: Frozen slots on WorldSlice might make subtype-based digest forgery impossible in the actual Python runtime.
discriminator: Subclass WorldSlice, override sha256() to return 64 zero hex characters, construct otherwise valid selected-atom slice, then require compile_qubo_projection to reject the subtype as non-exact.
minimal_repair: Replace the source_slice isinstance admission with an exact concrete-type check (type(source_slice) is WorldSlice) or compute the bound digest from a non-overridable canonical serializer over exact validated base fields. Add this falsifier as a regression. Review evaluate_qubo_assignment's analogous isinstance(projection, QuboProjection) boundary separately before promotion.
